clue.text: Manage to get round small group of trees

parts.note: to manage is to cope
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to walk all the way round a little wood.
explanation.walkthrough: S sits between the P and E of COPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thicket of small trees or undergrowth, often cut back for timber.

clue.text: Halved cash with street players

parts.note: the first half of CASH
ST is the standard abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Buskers splitting their takings down the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests street performers sharing money; 'players' is really the definition, a play's actors.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatre sense: the actors taking part in a production, taken together.

clue.text: Standard king's garden open to the public

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A royal garden that anyone may now walk in.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of king's reads as 'king is' joining the pieces, or simply the surface's possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: public grounds laid out with grass and trees for anyone to use.

clue.text: I bite idly resolving fitness for consumption

indicators.note: re-solving the letters: working them out into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone nibbling absent-mindedly while deciding whether the food is safe to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is a neat fit for the surface: idle biting is exactly how one tests edibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Edibility is the quality of being fit to eat.

clue.text: Tedium of moving bedroom

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: The dreary business of shifting house, one bedroom at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDROOM and BOREDOM share exactly the same seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom and tedium both mean weariness from dullness.

clue.text: Run into coastal shore as breakers do

parts.note: a beach is the shore of the coast
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Waves racing up onto the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes an action: waves (breakers) breach a sea wall, so the answer is a verb, what breakers do.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakers breach defences, breaking through them.

clue.text: Renegade and traitor, primarily

indicators.note: take what comes first in each word

parts.note: first letters of Renegade, And, Traitor

explanation.surface: A description of a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a rat is a renegade and traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is someone who deserts or betrays their side.

clue.text: Monstrous biocidal bats

indicators.note: batty, crazy: the letters go mad

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Horror-film bats that kill every living thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' reads as a noun, the creatures, but works as an adjective meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolic means devilish, monstrously wicked.

clue.text: Combative Italian dividing his city over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, the city with its insert sits over the time letter, above it
the abbreviation splits the city's name in two by sitting in its middle

parts.note: 'his' refers back to the Italian, and Milan is an Italian city

explanation.surface: An aggressive Italian splits his home city into factions for a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' puts IT into MILAN to give MILITAN, and 'over' places that above T in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Militant describes someone aggressively active in a cause, ready for confrontation.

clue.text: Leaders among sharks and rays eat fish

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters, taken from each of the three words that follow

parts.note: their first letters are S, A and R
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: The top sharks and rays feed on smaller fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders among' takes S, A and R from 'sharks and rays', including the little word 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily sea fish, often sold in tins.

clue.text: Follow around river path

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Directions for a walk: go along the riverside path.
explanation.walkthrough: R sits after the T of TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path, especially through countryside.

clue.text: Suffering minutes inside club, mostly loud

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub
FORTE is what 'loud' stands for
M is the abbreviation for minutes

explanation.surface: Enduring a few minutes in a nightclub where the music is far too loud.
explanation.walkthrough: Forte is the musical term for loud. 'Club' suggests a weapon or society; here it is a disco.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: physical or mental unease, a milder word for pain.

clue.text: Route maps ordered for Cheddar perhaps

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer by what it uses: a trap baited with cheese

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone ordering road maps before a trip to the English village of Cheddar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar is a Somerset village as well as the cheese, so the surface reads as travel planning; the cheese is the bait a mousetrap is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousetrap is typically baited with a piece of cheese such as Cheddar.

clue.text: Weapon armistice nearly knocked for six

indicators.note: knocked for six means thrown into disarray, so the remaining letters are rearranged
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of armistice is dropped

explanation.surface: A weapon causes a ceasefire agreement to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims ARMISTICE to ARMISTIC, and 'knocked for six' rearranges those letters. Knocked for six is a cricket idiom for being devastated.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved single-edged sword, a weapon of Middle Eastern origin.

clue.text: Totally striking, OK?

parts.note: workers on strike are out
right, as agreement, means OK

explanation.surface: A remark that something is completely stunning, seeking agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like impressive but means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb sense, as in 'rejected outright': completely, with nothing held back.

clue.text: Company briefly employing family member

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: using means employing

explanation.surface: A firm is taking on a relative for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a relative, the child of one's aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Swelling British association of workers

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a trade union

explanation.surface: A British trade union growing in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swelling' reads as an adjective about membership, but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunion is a painful swelling on the big toe joint.

clue.text: Bot making all get grief on Tinder initially

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

parts.words: making all get grief on Tinder
parts.note: first letters of making, all, get, grief, on, Tinder

explanation.surface: An automated account on a dating app that upsets everyone it matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bot' looks like a software robot; it is the larva of the botfly, a kind of maggot. Tinder is a dating app.
explanation.definitionFit: A bot is the maggot-like larva of the botfly.

clue.text: Sign of hesitation after my remark upset reveller

indicators.note: after places the hesitation sound behind the rearranged letters
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of my remark are jumbled

parts.note: er is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone pauses, umming, after an offensive comment upsets a partygoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MY REMARK into MERRYMAK, and 'after' places ER behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A merrymaker joins in festive celebration, which is what a reveller does.

clue.text: Want chessplayer to sacrifice bishop

indicators.note: give up a piece, as in chess

parts.note: one of the two sides in chess is Black
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; it is removed

explanation.surface: A chess player wanting to give up a bishop as a gambit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as desire, but here means need or shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and lack both mean a shortage of something.

clue.text: Tackle illicit drugs

definitions.meaning: the noun: equipment, as in fishing tackle
a slang term for illegal drugs

explanation.surface: An instruction to deal with the drug problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' is a verb in the surface but the noun equipment in the answer; fishing gear and the dealer's slang for drugs share the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear means equipment, and in slang, drugs.

clue.text: Mean drunk in snug

explanation.surface: A nasty drunk sitting in the pub's snug.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug is a small private room in a British pub, which makes the surface a pub scene; here 'snug' is an adjective, close-fitting, and 'in' only joins the meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One adjective covers all three senses: stingy with money, intoxicated in informal speech, and fitting closely.

clue.text: Bond regularly involved in strife

indicators.note: at regular intervals: the letters are taken at an even spacing, every second one
the letters are found within the next word

parts.note: the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of sTrIfE

explanation.surface: A James Bond film plot: the spy caught up in conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy; it is the definition, a link or tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a link that holds people together, as in family ties.

clue.text: Rubbish clothing at start of season

parts.note: garb is clothing
a season, like an age, is a period of time

explanation.surface: Awful new fashions appearing at the start of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of season' tempts a solver to take S, but nothing else then fits; 'season' is a stretch of time, an era.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, and the usual North American word for household waste.

clue.text: Climb-down on the subject of free entertainment?

parts.note: re means concerning
a treat is entertainment paid for by someone else

explanation.surface: Backing down on a promise of free entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the letter-heading word for 'regarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a climb-down, a backing away from a position.

clue.text: Certainly cutting for each card game

parts.note: per means for each
OK, certainly, agreed

explanation.surface: Someone cutting the deck before each hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' is a card-game word in the surface, but here it means going into.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the betting game of bluff played with five-card hands.
